about: What each tool lets AI Juggler observe and control, per layer, kept current (the maintainer, 2026-10-27). Research per tool family in the .md files beside this one; evidence labels per docs/research/EVIDENCE-STANDARD.md.

entries.product: Claude Code CLI

capabilities.name: Claude Agent SDK (TS/Python)
capabilities.how: Library that bundles its own Claude Code binary and speaks the CLI's stream-json control protocol.
capabilities.limits: Agent SDK page: 'Unless previously approved, Anthropic does not allow third party developers to offer claude.ai login or rate limits for their products'; adds Node plus a second ~274 MB binary. ADR-0022: not bundled.

capabilities.name: Headless stream-json control protocol
capabilities.how: claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --permission-prompt-tool stdio: can_use_tool, AskUserQuestion, interrupt, set_model, rate_limit_event, result.
capabilities.limits: Control protocol not a documented public contract; --bare (never reads OAuth) to become -p default; -p may be billed/classified as SDK use; skips workspace trust.

capabilities.name: PreToolUse defer (headless)
capabilities.how: In -p a PreToolUse hook returns permissionDecision 'defer'; result has stop_reason tool_deferred + deferred_tool_use; host resumes with claude -p --resume and answers via updatedInput. No timeout.
capabilities.limits: -p only; ignored in interactive sessions.

capabilities.name: Settings hooks (28 events)
capabilities.how: command/http/mcp_tool/prompt/agent handlers on SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, Notification, MessageDisplay, Stop, StopFailure, SessionEnd, Elicitation, etc.; block/rewrite/additionalContext/asyncRewake.
capabilities.limits: Only the last --settings applies; hooks held until workspace trust in interactive sessions; output capped at 10,000 chars.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: per-launch --settings overlay reports exact state via juggler-agent (claude_hooks)

capabilities.name: Answer a TUI permission prompt from a hook
capabilities.how: PermissionRequest hook may return decision allow/deny (+updatedPermissions); with a host 'whichever decides first applies'.
capabilities.limits: Whether a late hook decision closes the TUI dialog is unverified; lab saw the dialog drawn before the hook started. Must carry only the user's click (D-28).

capabilities.name: Status line JSON
capabilities.how: statusLine command receives JSON incl. rate_limits.five_hour/seven_day (Pro/Max), cost, context_window, transcript_path.
capabilities.limits: Interactive only; debounced; rate_limits only for subscribers.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: status line wrapper records rate_limits for sessions it starts

capabilities.name: Plugins and marketplaces
capabilities.how: Plugin = skills, commands, agents, hooks, MCP, LSP, bin/, settings(agent, subagentStatusLine), themes, output styles, channels, monitors, workflows, mods; --plugin-dir/--plugin-url per session; CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS env.
capabilities.limits: Installing into a profile writes the user's settings (needs consent); org policy can restrict marketplaces.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: ships plugins/claude-code (ai-juggler MCP server + pool-tasks skill)

capabilities.name: Plugin monitors
capabilities.how: monitors/monitors.json: a background shell command per session whose output lines reach Claude as notifications.
capabilities.limits: Interactive sessions only (not -p); full user permissions; whether a line wakes an idle session is unverified.

capabilities.name: Mods (in-process JS hooks)
capabilities.how: Plugin hooks module: tool.call/tool.check (hold/allow/deny), $.prompt.submit (start a turn), $.turn.abort, $.session.messages/usage (rateLimits with resetsAt), $.session.send, $.process.spawn, $.http.fetch, panes.
capabilities.limits: On by default from 2.1.287; cannot change the permission prompt; 10 s own-time per event; allowManagedModsOnly/sec-default can block; full user permissions, so never auto-answer.

capabilities.name: MCP server tools/resources/prompts
capabilities.how: Our stdio server via --mcp-config, .mcp.json, claude mcp add (local/project/user) or a plugin; resources via @, prompts as commands, roots/list answered, list_changed honoured.
capabilities.limits: 25k-token output cap (MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS), >50k chars saved to file unless _meta anthropic/maxResultSizeChars; idle timeout 30 min stdio; calls >2 min backgrounded.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: agent bridge (juggler-agent --mcp) for pools, messages, tasks

capabilities.name: Tool annotations and _meta
capabilities.how: readOnlyHint (parallel), idempotentHint (retry), _meta anthropic/requiresUserInteraction (prompt every call), anthropic/alwaysLoad, anthropic/maxResultSizeChars.
capabilities.limits: Claude Code-specific _meta keys.

capabilities.name: MCP elicitation (ask the user)
capabilities.how: elicitation/create in form and url modes, declared {form:{},url:{}} to user-configured servers (>=2.1.287); Elicitation/ElicitationResult hooks.
capabilities.limits: Inside MCP tasks served only in interactive terminal sessions; url mode argument cap ~8,000 chars.

capabilities.name: MCP sampling
capabilities.how: Not offered.
capabilities.limits: Not found in Claude Code docs; claude.com: 'Claude doesn't yet support ... Sampling'.

capabilities.name: Channels (server pushes into a running session)
capabilities.how: Server declares experimental claude/channel and emits notifications/claude/channel {content, meta}; arrives as <channel> in the live session.
capabilities.limits: Research preview: allowlisted plugins only; custom needs --dangerously-load-development-channels with interactive confirm; ignored in -p/SDK; v2 runtime won't register a 2026-07-28 server (MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION=legacy); claude.ai or Console sign-in; Team/Enterprise channelsEnabled.

capabilities.name: Channel permission relay
capabilities.how: With claude/channel/permission the server receives permission_request {request_id, tool_name, description, input_preview} and answers notifications/claude/channel/permission {request_id, behavior}; first answer (terminal or relay) wins.
capabilities.limits: Same preview limits as channels; tool approvals only, not trust or MCP consent; sanitized and redacted previews.

capabilities.name: Cross-session inbox socket
capabilities.how: Per-session Unix socket exported as CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET (+ CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN) to hooks; docs invite a script or hook to post into a session; delivered between tool calls or as a new turn.
capabilities.limits: Only the auth line is documented; the message line format comes from a binary debug hint; crossSessionInbound hold/refuse; cannot approve; 30 s line timeout; not bound in --bare.

capabilities.name: SendMessage / ListAgents between sessions
capabilities.how: Claude-to-Claude messages across local, background and Remote Control sessions (>=2.1.224).
capabilities.limits: Model-initiated; inbound controls apply; messages count as usage.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: not used (AI Juggler pools use its own MCP tools)

capabilities.name: claude agents --json
capabilities.how: Supported JSON of live sessions: state, status (busy/waiting/idle), waitingFor, sessionId, pid, cwd; no TTY needed.
capabilities.limits: Whether it starts the supervisor is unknown; per CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR.

capabilities.name: --bg / attach / supervisor
capabilities.how: claude --bg, claude attach/logs/stop/respawn/rm; supervisor restarts sessions.
capabilities.limits: Permission prompts answerable only by attaching; AI Juggler would not own the processes (ADR-0010).

capabilities.name: OSC 7501 program status in the PTY
capabilities.how: A terminal that answers the OSC 7501;? probe gets state=working|blocked|done (kind, progress, title/msg base64) for each interactive session.
capabilities.limits: Needs >=2.1.295; not in tmux or background sessions, or with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE; payload format from the binary.

capabilities.name: TUI under a PTY
capabilities.how: Real TUI in AI Juggler's terminal: Esc and Ctrl+C interrupt, queued input, large pastes collapse to [Pasted text #N].
capabilities.limits: Screen parsing is heuristic; ToS fine (unmodified binary, user's own sign-in).
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: default runtime for Claude sessions it starts

capabilities.name: Insert input into a session
capabilities.how: Driven: stream-json user message. Terminal: inbox socket, mod $.prompt.submit, channel notification, monitor output; deep link prefill.
capabilities.limits: AI Juggler never types into a PTY by rule; each terminal route has preview or format caveats.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: driven sessions only (send_turn); terminal sessions pull messages via MCP

capabilities.name: Read output and state
capabilities.how: stream-json events; hooks (MessageDisplay, Stop last_assistant_message, transcript_path); status line; agents --json; mods $.session.messages.
capabilities.limits: Transcript JSONL 'internal to Claude Code and changes between versions'.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: transcript tails, hooks and stream events

capabilities.name: Transcripts on disk
capabilities.how: D/projects/<cwd slug>/<session>.jsonl plus subagents/, tool-results/, file-history.
capabilities.limits: Format internal, may break on any release; not encrypted; 30-day cleanup.

capabilities.name: sessions/<pid>.json live markers
capabilities.how: Per-running-session file with status, sessionId, cwd and entrypoint.
capabilities.limits: Undocumented shape; agents --json is the supported route.

capabilities.name: OpenTelemetry export
capabilities.how: CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY + OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*: metrics (tokens, cost, sessions) and events (tool_decision, api_request, api_error, permission_mode_changed, hooks, compaction).
capabilities.limits: Content attributes off unless OTEL_LOG_* set; needs a local OTLP receiver.

capabilities.name: claude-cli:// deep links
capabilities.how: claude-cli://open?q=&cwd=&repo= opens a new terminal with the prompt filled in (never sent; 5,000 chars).
capabilities.limits: Handler registered only after the first interactive prompt; disableDeepLinkRegistration.

capabilities.name: claude --desktop
capabilities.how: claude --desktop [--continue|--resume <id>] opens the folder or session in Claude Desktop.
capabilities.limits: Subscription sign-in; >=2.1.285; won't move a session open elsewhere.

capabilities.name: Resume / fork / session id
capabilities.how: --resume <id|path>, --continue, --session-id, --fork-session, --resume-session-at (headless).
capabilities.limits: One writer at a time; -p sessions hidden from the picker.

capabilities.name: Plan limits with reset times
capabilities.how: Status line rate_limits; stream-json rate_limit_event; mod $.session.usage().rateLimits; claude -p /usage (text).
capabilities.limits: Pro/Max only; rate_limit_event reports the window in force.

capabilities.name: Remote Control
capabilities.how: Drives a local session from claude.ai/mobile via Anthropic's API.
capabilities.limits: No local API for third parties; outbound to Anthropic only.

capabilities.name: claude mcp serve
capabilities.how: Claude Code's tools as a stdio MCP server.
capabilities.limits: The client must do its own confirmations.

capabilities.name: A session's subagents and their conversations
capabilities.how: <project>/<session>/subagents/agent-<id>.meta.json (agentType, description, toolUseId, spawnDepth, parentAgentId, requestShape, stoppedByUser) and agent-<id>.jsonl (the subagent's own conversation, every line isSidechain) beside the session transcript; the Agent call's tool_result (toolUseResult.status completed / async_launched, agentId) and, for a background one, the <task-notification> (<task-id> = agent id, <status> completed|failed|killed|stopped) queued (queue-operation, queued_command attachment) and given to the session (user line, origin.kind task-notification). A nested one's status is in its parent subagent's transcript.
capabilities.limits: File formats are internal and undocumented; checked against this Mac's records (field names and counts only): 180 subagents in 10 sessions, every one's end found. 30-day cleanup applies to the folder too.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: Subagents tab (AJ-E1520, 0.2): claude_subagents lists them read-only; conversations open in the session page's chat view

entries.product: Claude desktop app (Chat, Code tab, Cowork)

capabilities.name: claude:// links (documented)
capabilities.how: claude://claude.ai/new?q=, claude://claude.ai/chat/{id}, claude://claude.ai/project/{id}, claude://code/new?q=&folder=, claude://cowork/new?q=&folder=&file=, SSH form code/new?ssh_host=...
capabilities.limits: Prefill only, never sends; folder confirmation always; q cut at ~14,000 chars.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: not used (bundle id known for Go to it)

capabilities.name: claude://resume?session=<id> (undocumented)
capabilities.how: Built by the CLI for claude --desktop --resume; also claude://claude.ai/<path>.
capabilities.limits: Undocumented (binary only); behaviour for an existing Code-tab session unknown; Desktop >=1.1.9669.

capabilities.name: AppleScript / Apple Events
capabilities.how: No scripting dictionary in the bundle.
capabilities.limits: NSAppleEventsUsageDescription is for Claude controlling other apps.

capabilities.name: Accessibility tree automation
capabilities.how: Electron window AX tree.
capabilities.limits: Driving chat would be 'automated or non-human means' under the Consumer Terms; fragile; needs an Accessibility grant.

capabilities.name: Desktop app local socket/IPC
capabilities.how: None documented.
capabilities.limits: Code-tab sessions run embedded Claude Code, so its inbox socket and hooks apply there (inferred).

capabilities.name: Headless / scripting the Code tab
capabilities.how: 'Desktop is interactive only'; --print and SDK not available.
capabilities.limits: Use the CLI for scripting.

capabilities.name: Desktop Extensions (.mcpb/.dxt)
capabilities.how: Zip of a local stdio MCP server + manifest.json, one-click install; user_config UI; Node bundled.
capabilities.limits: User installs it; directory no longer accepts MCPB submissions (ship in a plugin).

capabilities.name: claude_desktop_config.json MCP servers
capabilities.how: Local servers load into Chat and Code-tab sessions; Desktop's definition wins on a name clash.
capabilities.limits: Writing it is a user-config write that needs consent.

capabilities.name: MCP tools in Chat/Cowork
capabilities.how: Tools, prompts, resources; text and image results; MCP Apps UI.
capabilities.limits: ~150,000 chars per result, 240 s per call; remote connectors go through Anthropic's cloud.

capabilities.name: MCP sampling / resource subscriptions
capabilities.how: Not supported.
capabilities.limits: 'Claude doesn't yet support ... Sampling'.

capabilities.name: MCP elicitation in Chat
capabilities.how: Not documented for Chat.
capabilities.limits: Code tab follows Claude Code.

capabilities.name: Channels in the Code tab
capabilities.how: Desktop changelog mentions <channel-message> turns.
capabilities.limits: No Desktop way to pass --channels found.

capabilities.name: Plugins in Chat / Cowork / Code tab
capabilities.how: Chat: skills and commands only. Cowork: skills, commands, agents, hooks, local MCP. Code tab: full Claude Code plugins.
capabilities.limits: Chat and Cowork read plugins from the account; Code tab from the machine.

capabilities.name: Mods in the Code tab
capabilities.how: Same mods API as the CLI (state, usage, $.prompt.submit, tool.check) inside Desktop Code sessions.
capabilities.limits: Code tab >=2.1.286; not WSL; installed as a plugin (consent); org guards.

capabilities.name: Hooks in the Code tab
capabilities.how: ~/.claude/settings.json hooks and plugin hooks apply to Code-tab sessions.
capabilities.limits: No per-launch flags in Desktop, so AI Juggler's --settings overlay cannot reach them.

capabilities.name: claude-code-sessions/.../local_<id>.json
capabilities.how: The app's per-session file with status word, cliSessionId, cwd, title.
capabilities.limits: Undocumented; may change with any Desktop release.

capabilities.name: Code-tab transcripts
capabilities.how: Embedded CLI writes projects/<cwd>/<id>.jsonl; found via cliSessionId.
capabilities.limits: Internal format.

capabilities.name: Read a Chat conversation locally
capabilities.how: Chats live on Anthropic's servers.
capabilities.limits: Reading app caches is off-limits.

capabilities.name: Insert a message
capabilities.how: Chat/Code/Cowork: prefilled links only (user sends). Code tab: mod $.prompt.submit or inbox socket (inferred).
capabilities.limits: No sanctioned send for Chat.

capabilities.name: Move a CLI session into Desktop
capabilities.how: claude --desktop --resume <id>, or /desktop; Desktop /resume lists CLI sessions.
capabilities.limits: Subscription sign-in; session must not be open elsewhere.

capabilities.name: Dispatch / Cowork API
capabilities.how: None for third parties.
capabilities.limits: Dispatch: Pro/Max only.

capabilities.name: Cowork/Desktop OpenTelemetry
capabilities.how: Cowork monitoring via OTel for organizations; the Code tab honours Claude Code OTel env from settings (inferred).
capabilities.limits: Admin-oriented; not verified for personal plans.

capabilities.name: The Code tab's sessions' subagents
capabilities.how: The Code tab runs the same Claude Code on the same projects folder, so its sessions' subagents/ folders read as the CLI's.
capabilities.limits: Chat-tab conversations are kept on Anthropic's servers: no subagent record on this Mac.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: Subagents tab, through the conversations index (same reader as the CLI's)

entries.product: Codex CLI (codex-cli, openai/codex)

capabilities.name: App-server JSON-RPC
capabilities.how: codex app-server --listen stdio:// (newline JSON-RPC 2.0 without the jsonrpc field); initialize{clientInfo,capabilities} then initialized; 105 stable client requests, 10 server requests, 85 notifications in 0.163.0 (172/11 with experimentalApi). Threads (start/resume/fork/read/list/turns/list/items/list/compact/revert/archive/name), turns (start/steer/interrupt), approvals and questions as server requests, account/rateLimits/read + updated, thread/tokenUsage/updated, MCP/skills/hooks/plugins/config methods.
capabilities.limits: 'The app-server command and WebSocket transport are experimental and aren't supported for production workloads'; schemas match one version exactly; full-history hydration deprecated (use excludeTurns + thread/turns/list); unix:// speaks WebSocket (lab 2026-10-25). Terms: local/open-source apps may use app-server auth; never commercial/hosted.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: Driven Codex sessions (D-40, ADR-0022): one stdio app-server per session; uses thread/start|resume, turn/start|steer|interrupt, thread/compact/start, model/list, rate limits, token usage, approvals, requestUserInput (crates/juggler-adapters/src/codex_appserver)

capabilities.name: Schema generation
capabilities.how: codex app-server generate-json-schema --out DIR [--experimental]; generate-ts --out DIR. Offline, needs only an existing CODEX_HOME.
capabilities.limits: Output is version-specific; experimental surface gated.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: Pinned surface fixture surface-0.163.0.json; schema mismatch falls back to the PTY

capabilities.name: Live limits with resets
capabilities.how: account/rateLimits/read and account/rateLimits/updated (notify, 'emitted whenever a user's ChatGPT rate limits change'); rateLimitsByLimitId{primary,secondary{usedPercent,windowDurationMins,resetsAt},credits,planType,rateLimitReachedType}; account/usage/read.
capabilities.limits: Window identity by windowDurationMins only; some accounts report only the weekly window (lab). Rollout token_count.rate_limits remains the local fallback.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: Used for driven sessions; rollout reader for others

capabilities.name: Approvals and questions
capabilities.how: Server requests item/commandExecution/requestApproval (accept, acceptForSession, acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment, applyNetworkPolicyAmendment, decline, cancel), item/fileChange/requestApproval, item/permissions/requestApproval (scope turn|session), item/tool/requestUserInput (experimental; 1-3 questions, autoResolutionMs lets a host auto-resolve), mcpServer/elicitation/request; serverRequest/resolved to every subscriber.
capabilities.limits: Two subscribers both get the request, first answer wins (lab 2). requestUserInput not sent with experimentalApi=false in 0.163.0. approval_policy 'untrusted' is now documented as unsupported (use on-request or never).
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: Needs you answers in AI Juggler (user's answer only; never autoResolution)

capabilities.name: Inject model-visible items
capabilities.how: thread/inject_items {threadId, items: raw Responses API items} appends to a loaded thread's model-visible history without starting a user turn (stable in 0.163.0 schema).
capabilities.limits: Loaded threads only; items are raw Responses API objects (shape risk); what the user sees in other clients is unverified (U).

capabilities.name: Client-provided tools
capabilities.how: thread/start dynamicTools [DynamicToolSpec]; the model's call arrives as server request item/tool/call {threadId,turnId,callId,namespace,tool,arguments}; client answers {success, contentItems}.
capabilities.limits: Experimental (capabilities.experimentalApi=true required); names must follow Responses API rules and avoid reserved namespaces.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: not used (codec ignores item/tool/call; bridge uses MCP juggler-agent instead)

capabilities.name: Goal mode
capabilities.how: thread/goal/set|get|clear {objective,status,tokenBudget}; thread/goal/updated|cleared; same state as /goal in the TUI.
capabilities.limits: origin field: 'Missing provenance does not supply user authorization.'

capabilities.name: Queued messages
capabilities.how: CLI: codex queue --thread <id|name> --message TEXT [--remote ADDR] (thread/queue/add through the local app-server daemon or a remote server; refuses --no-daemon); app-server thread/queue/add|list|update|delete|reorder|start, thread/queue/changed.
capabilities.limits: thread/queue/* are experimental; queue persisted in the state DB; no images. Whether a non-daemon server (Codex Desktop, AI Juggler's stdio server) drains items queued elsewhere: U.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: not used (AI Juggler queues E18 deliveries itself and sends at turn boundaries)

capabilities.name: Shared app-server daemon and --remote
capabilities.how: Since 0.157 the TUI uses a per-CODEX_HOME daemon (socket under $CODEX_HOME/app-server-control/); clients: codex --remote unix://[PATH] | ws:// | wss://, codex agents (command center), codex queue, resume/fork/archive/delete/unarchive --remote; codex app-server proxy --sock PATH proxies stdio to the control socket; codex app-server daemon start|stop|restart|version.
capabilities.limits: Daemon is Codex's process, not AI Juggler's (ADR-0010/0022 rejected attaching for now); --no-daemon can't combine with --remote; non-loopback ws listeners unauthenticated by default during rollout.
sources: codex --help; codex app-server help daemon; codex app-server help proxy (0.163.0)
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: not used; AI Juggler passes --no-daemon for terminal launches and runs its own stdio server for driven ones

capabilities.name: codex exec --json
capabilities.how: codex exec --json PROMPT (JSONL: thread.started, turn.started, item.*, turn.completed{usage}, turn.failed, error); -o, --output-schema, --ephemeral, --ignore-user-config, exec resume|fork.
capabilities.limits: Cannot answer approvals; for one-shots and CI.

capabilities.name: @openai/codex-sdk (TypeScript)
capabilities.how: Node 18+; Codex().startThread().run(); resumeThread(id); spawns codex exec --experimental-json.
capabilities.limits: No approval callback (wraps exec); needs Node; bundling rejected (ADR-0022).

capabilities.name: openai-codex (Python)
capabilities.how: pip install openai-codex (0.163.0 on PyPI); JSON-RPC client of app-server with a pinned CLI runtime; Sandbox presets.
capabilities.limits: Default approval handler accepts command and file-change approvals (client.py _default_approval_handler) unless a handler is passed; Python runtime not bundled.

capabilities.name: codex mcp-server
capabilities.how: Removed 2026-09-05 after deprecation 2026-08-24; app-server is the replacement.
capabilities.limits: codex mcp-server now falls through to the main help (0.163.0).

capabilities.name: Plugins and marketplaces
capabilities.how: Plugin = folder with plugin.json (portable Agent Plugins schema) or .codex-plugin/plugin.json; bundles skills/, .mcp.json servers, .app.json apps, hooks (hooks/hooks.json or manifest). Marketplaces: ~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json, $REPO/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json, codex plugin marketplace add owner/repo|git|path; enable per project with [plugins."name@marketplace"]. App-server plugin/list|install|read|uninstall, marketplace/*.
capabilities.limits: Plugin hooks need hash-based trust; plugin MCP servers' transport is fixed by the plugin, user config can only toggle/tool-policy them.

capabilities.name: Skills
capabilities.how: SKILL.md folders: $CWD/.agents/skills up to repo root, $HOME/.agents/skills, /etc/codex/skills, bundled system skills, plus plugin skills; skills.config enable overrides; app-server skills/list, skills/changed, skills/extraRoots/set.
capabilities.limits: Shared by every CODEX_HOME (~/.agents is per user, not per home).
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: Inventory and Claude to Codex skill translation (switching-capabilities.md)

capabilities.name: Custom prompts
capabilities.how: $CODEX_HOME/prompts/*.md
capabilities.limits: Deprecated 2026-01-22 in favour of skills; 0.164.0 adds /presets slots.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: Translated in switching (Codex prompt to Claude command)

capabilities.name: AGENTS.md
capabilities.how: $CODEX_HOME/AGENTS.override.md or AGENTS.md, then repo-root-to-cwd AGENTS.md; project_doc_fallback_filenames, project_doc_max_bytes.
capabilities.limits: Read into the first turn only.

capabilities.name: Lifecycle hooks
capabilities.how: ~/.codex/hooks.json, inline [hooks] in config.toml, <repo>/.codex/hooks.json, plugin hooks. Events: SessionStart, SessionEnd, PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PostCompact, UserPromptSubmit, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, Stop, Interrupt. Handlers: command or mcp_tool. Stdin JSON has session_id, transcript_path, cwd, turn_id, permission_mode. PermissionRequest can allow/deny; Stop can return decision:block with reason = a new continuation prompt; async hooks add additionalContext at the next safe point.
capabilities.limits: 'Non-managed hooks must be reviewed and trusted before they run' (trust recorded per hook hash via /hooks); --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust is for vetted automation only; project hooks only in trusted projects; timeouts default 600 s (SessionEnd/Interrupt 1-3 s).
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: not used for Codex (used for Claude terminal sessions)

capabilities.name: notify program
capabilities.how: notify = ["prog", ...] runs on agent-turn-complete with JSON {type, thread-id, turn-id, cwd, input-messages, last-assistant-message}.
capabilities.limits: User-level config only (ignored in project config); no approval/question event; carries message text.

capabilities.name: Our MCP server's tools
capabilities.how: [mcp_servers.<name>] command/args/env/env_vars/cwd (stdio) or url + bearer_token_env_var/http_headers/env_http_headers/http_headers_helper/oauth (streamable HTTP); codex mcp add NAME -- CMD | --url; per-launch -c mcp_servers.x.*; enabled_tools/disabled_tools; default_tools_approval_mode auto|prompt|writes|approve and tools.<t>.approval_mode; tools.<t>.output_token_limit; server instructions (first 512 chars matter).
capabilities.limits: startup_timeout_sec 10, tool_timeout_sec 60 defaults; mcp_optional_startup_grace_ms 1000; no SSE/WebSocket transport; project servers only in trusted projects.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: juggler-agent bridge injected per launch with -c mcp_servers.juggler.* (codex_bridge.rs): whoami, pool_roster, set_status

capabilities.name: Our MCP server's resources
capabilities.how: Model tools list_mcp_resources, list_mcp_resource_templates, read_mcp_resource; app-server mcpServer/resource/read and mcpServerStatus/list (detail full).
capabilities.limits: Model must choose to read them; resource-updated notifications are only logged.

capabilities.name: Our MCP server's prompts
capabilities.how: No prompts surface found; prompt_list_changed is only logged by the client handler.

entries.product: OpenCode CLI/TUI (opencode) - two live lines: v1 (npm opencode-ai) and v2 (npm @opencode/cli)
entries.version_source: https://registry.npmjs.org/opencode-ai ; https://registry.npmjs.org/@opencode/cli ; https://opencode.ai/update/api/latest/cli/npm ; https://api.github.com/repos/anomalyco/opencode/releases ; opencode not installed on this Mac (command not found)
entries.notes: Two live lines: v1 (npm `opencode-ai`, the line AI Juggler's adapter targets) and v2 (npm `@opencode/cli`, 2.2.0 on 2026-10-27, a shared per-user service on port 49374). The feed tracks v1.

capabilities.name: v1 HTTP server (opencode serve / TUI --port)
capabilities.how: opencode serve [--port 4096 --hostname 127.0.0.1]; OpenAPI 3.1 at /doc; /session (create/list/get/delete/update/children/todo/init/fork/abort/diff/summarize/revert/unrevert/permissions), /session/:id/message, /session/:id/prompt_async (204), /session/:id/command, /session/:id/shell, /event + /global/event SSE, /tui/* control. The v1 TUI serves in-process (worker, url opencode.internal) and listens on the network only when --port/--hostname/--mdns is passed
capabilities.limits: Basic auth only if OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD is set: without it the localhost server is open. Two processes on one DB do not share events. No stability promise

capabilities.name: v2 shared background service + HttpApi
capabilities.how: There is one shared service per user (opencode serve --service), discovered through $XDG_STATE_HOME/opencode/service.json (url, pid, version, password; mode 0600). The default port is 49374 (0xC0DE), set per account with $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/service.json or `opencode service set port`. 156 operations under /api/*: session create/list/get/prompt/synthetic/interrupt/fork/compact/command/shell/model/permission reply/inbox/active, /api/event SSE, a durable /api/experimental/session/:id/log (after=seq, follow=true), /api/pty WebSockets. Also --standalone (private server) and --server <url>. `opencode api <operationId>` calls it from the CLI
capabilities.limits: The spec calls itself 'Experimental HttpApi surface' (info.version 0.0.1). /api/event is volatile: no replay, slow consumers dropped. Fixed default port: a second XDG-isolated service collides ('Managed service port ... already in use'). service.json holds a password (a credential)
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: not used as an API. Managed accounts on 2.x launch every TUI, run and auth login with --standalone (a private server on a system-chosen port, leased to the TUI's stdin, nothing written or read); the default folder used in place joins the user's shared service, as their own opencode does (opencode/service.rs)

capabilities.name: TypeScript SDK / client
capabilities.how: v1: @opencode-ai/sdk 1.19.4 (createOpencode / createOpencodeClient; session.*, event.subscribe, tui.appendPrompt/submitPrompt, auth.set; /v2 sub-client adds structured output). v2: @opencode/client 2.2.0 (OpenCode.make({baseUrl}), Service.discover/ensure) and @opencode/sdk 2.2.0 (embedded host, no HTTP listener)
capabilities.limits: No stability statement. v1 and v2 contracts are incompatible ('The server API and clients have new contracts'). These are JS packages, so a Rust app speaks HTTP to the OpenAPI directly

capabilities.name: opencode run --format json
capabilities.how: run [message..] with -c/-s/--fork/-m/--agent/-f/--title/--format json; v1 also --attach <url>, --port; v2 uses the global --server/--standalone
capabilities.limits: v2 run joins the shared service by default. JSON event schema not documented as stable
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: Headless launch mode: `run [--standalone on 2.x managed] --format json [--model=] -- <prompt>`

capabilities.name: Attach a TUI to a server
capabilities.how: v1: `opencode attach [url] --dir -s -c --fork -p/--password`, or TUI --port/--hostname. v2: global `--server <url>`; local clients attach to the shared service automatically
capabilities.limits: v2 has no `attach` subcommand. The TUI and Desktop share the service, so both see the same sessions live

capabilities.name: Agent Client Protocol
capabilities.how: `opencode acp` over stdio JSON-RPC (ACP v1). v2: session new/load (replay)/resume/fork/list/close/delete, cancel, set_config_option (model/effort/mode), permissions, form elicitation, client-passed stdio/HTTP MCP servers, usage_update notifications, `--login` terminal auth
capabilities.limits: Runs a private server, not the shared service. One prompt at a time per session. No MCP OAuth/SSE via ACP. v1 docs: /undo and /redo are unsupported

capabilities.name: Server plugins (JS/TS)
capabilities.how: v1: modules in .opencode/plugins or ~/.config/opencode/plugins or npm `plugin` []; input {client (SDK), project, directory, worktree, serverUrl, $}; hooks event, config, auth, chat.message, chat.params, chat.headers, permission.ask (set allow/deny), command.execute.before, tool.execute.before/after, shell.env, tool.definition, experimental.* (system/messages transform, compaction). v2: Plugin.define({id, setup(ctx)}); ctx is a full server client; hooks session prompt/context/compaction/generate/title/model.request/http.*, permission evaluate, shell create.before, tool execute.before/after; transforms; ctx.session.synthetic/prompt; ctx.event.subscribe; RPC (Rpc.define, callable at /api/rpc/{rpcID}/{method}, events rpc.<id>.<name>)
capabilities.limits: v1 plugins do not run in v2 ('must be ported'). A plugin runs arbitrary code with the user's rights, so installing one is a config change that needs consent
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: not used (import copies config but skips installed plugin packages)

capabilities.name: TUI plugins
capabilities.how: v2: ./tui export or cli.json `plugins`; commands/keymaps, UI slots, toasts, dialogs, routes, context.client, context.data (sessions, messages, permissions) with listen
capabilities.limits: Only shows inside the TUI. Config moved from tui.json to cli.json

capabilities.how: v1: `mcp.<name>` {type local command[]/environment | remote url/headers/oauth, enabled, timeout}; client declares roots; tools + prompts + resources catalog; tools/list_changed handled. v2: `mcp.servers.<name>` (disabled, codemode, protocol legacy|auto|2026-07-28; startup/catalog/execution timeouts); tools as <server>_<tool> (Code Mode by default); prompts as /<server>:<prompt>; resources via list_mcp_resources/read_mcp_resource; server instructions added to the system prompt; OAuth with PKCE, CIMD and DCR

capabilities.how: v2: form and URL elicitation, shown as a form or link; dismissing cancels. v1: not declared (issue #23066)
capabilities.limits: v2 elicitations are Location-scoped, not session-scoped. Secret-collecting forms are never sent to ACP clients

capabilities.how: No MCP path found. The alternatives are the API (v2 POST /api/session/:id/synthetic or /prompt with delivery steer|queue; v1 prompt_async or noReply prompt), a plugin (v2 ctx.session.synthetic), or the experimental v2 client-hosted MCP over WebSocket (/api/experimental/client-mcp), which exposes tools only

capabilities.name: Session store (SQLite)
capabilities.how: $XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/opencode.db in WAL mode. v1: session/message/part tables with JSON data. v2: session_v2, session_message, session_inbox, plus a durable `event` table and credential/account tables. `opencode db [query]`, `session list --format json`, `export`
capabilities.limits: The old storage/ JSON layout is legacy (migrated). The schema churns: v2 had 54 migrations, the newest 2026-10-25 (drop_session_allowance, drop_session_pending). The vendor says 'Don't edit the database directly'. Credentials share the file

capabilities.name: Read live output
capabilities.how: v1: GET /event SSE (message.part.updated, session.idle/status/error, permission.asked...) when AI Juggler started the server or TUI with --port. v2: /api/event (session.text.delta, tool.*, session.idle, session.status, usage.updated...) and the durable /api/experimental/session/:id/log?after=&follow=true. Both: polling the DB
capabilities.limits: The v1 TUI without --port exposes no events to other processes. The v2 event stream is volatile; the log endpoint is experimental

capabilities.name: Insert a prompt into a running session
capabilities.how: v1: POST /session/:id/prompt_async, or /tui/append-prompt + /tui/submit-prompt (drives the visible TUI), on a server AI Juggler started with a known password. v2: POST /api/session/:id/prompt {text, delivery: steer|queue, resume}, /synthetic, /interrupt?resume=; the TUI and Desktop render it live because they share the service
capabilities.limits: Needs the server URL and password. For the user's default v2 service that means reading service.json (a credential), which needs a maintainer ruling; managed accounts can set their own password. v2 has no /tui/* endpoints

capabilities.name: Wrap the TUI in a PTY
capabilities.how: Deterministic parts: argv (`--session <id>`, `--prompt=<text>`, `-c`, `--fork`; v1 `--model`, v2 model via OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT), env/XDG isolation, exit. The v1 home route auto-submits --prompt once the model is ready. Typing into the composer works, but reading state from the full-screen OpenTUI render is heuristic
capabilities.limits: Scraping the screen is fragile; prefer the DB/API. Whether v2 --prompt submits or only fills the composer is unconfirmed
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: Interactive/Primed/Resume launches with needs_pty=true; `auth login` in a PTY

capabilities.name: Per-session shell environment (v2)
capabilities.how: PUT /api/session/:id/environment {variables} replaces the env used by local shell commands of that session; service config `env` sets service env
capabilities.limits: Replaces the whole env. Untested
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: not used (XDG isolation vars leak into agent tools today)

capabilities.how: GET /api/experimental/usage/limits?location= returns the signed-in Console workspace's Go allowance meters (rolling, weekly, monthly) and Console budgets, or null when not signed in

capabilities.how: v2: several saved credentials per provider, one active; `opencode auth list` / `opencode auth switch <provider> <label|id>` / logout; API /api/credential (+ /activate); stored in opencode.db. v1: one entry per provider in auth.json

capabilities.name: Licence and terms
capabilities.how: Repo is MIT (anomalyco/opencode, 222k stars; sst/opencode redirects with 301). npm packages are MIT. The OpenCode ToS (Zen/Go/Console) bars multiple accounts to circumvent limits and 'automatically or programmatically extracts data or Output'

capabilities.name: A session's subagents (child sessions)
capabilities.how: A subagent is a child session: parent_id in session (1.x) / session_v2 (2.x), its agent column the agent, its title '<description> (@<agent> subagent)'. 1.x: the parent's task tool part (state.metadata.sessionId, state.status pending|running|completed|error, state.time.start/end); a background one completes its part at once, so the child's last message (error; time.completed, finish) says. 2.x: the child's idle_outcome succeeded|failed|interrupted at time_idle. API: GET /session/:id/children (1.x), GET /api/session?parentID= (2.x).
capabilities.limits: session list --format json lists top-level sessions only, export one session without children; both run migrations and write logs. The HTTP routes need an OpenCode server on the user's store. Conversations are message/part rows, not a transcript file.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: Subagents tab (AJ-E1520, 0.2): opencode_subagents lists them from the store, read-only (immutable when OpenCode is closed); conversations not shown yet

capabilities.name: Print mode, stream-json
capabilities.how: `kimi -p <prompt> [--output-format text|stream-json]`; stream-json = one JSON object per line: assistant messages (with tool_calls), tool messages, and meta lines (system.version, session.resume_hint, turn.step.retrying). Auto permission policy; static deny rules still apply. Goal mode exits 0/3/6.

Project MCP servers off unless the workspace is trusted (KIMI_CODE_TRUST_WORKSPACE=1). Terms: membership is 'interactive use only'; 'Don't use Kimi Code for non-interactive automation'.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: LaunchMode::Headless -> `-p <prompt> --output-format stream-json`, refused for membership (interactive_only) accounts; allowed for Platform API-key accounts

capabilities.name: Agent Client Protocol server
capabilities.how: `kimi acp`: JSON-RPC on stdio. Core 3/3 and session 11/11 methods: session/new (cwd, mcpServers, additionalDirectories), load (replays history), resume (no replay), list (sessions on disk, by cwd), fork, close, delete, prompt (text/image/resource), cancel, set_mode, set_config_option (model/thinking/mode), set_model ext. Reverse RPC: session/update, request_permission, fs/*, terminal/*, elicitation/create (form).
capabilities.limits: Not implemented: providers/*, nes/*, document/*, elicitation/complete. Auth via terminal method (`kimi login`). Sessions created over ACP land in the same session store (resumable in the TUI). One session cannot be written by two processes (lock).

capabilities.name: Local REST + WebSocket server (`kimi web`)
capabilities.how: `kimi web [--no-open --port]` on 127.0.0.1:58627+, bearer token in $KIMI_CODE_HOME/server.token (also printed); instances under server/instances/. REST: sessions CRUD/fork/compact/undo/abort/archive/takeover, prompts (submit, steer, abort, queue), approvals and questions (list/answer), tasks, MCP servers, plugins, workspaces/trust, fs, oauth/usage. WS /api/v1/ws: subscribe to session events (turn.started, assistant.delta, tool.call.started, tool.result, turn.ended). Live specs at /openapi.json and /asyncapi.json.
capabilities.limits: Marked experimental: 'interface stability is not guaranteed'. Drives only sessions loaded in that server process; a session held by a TUI returns 40931 (occupied); :takeover only when the holder is gone. Reading the token file is reading a credential-like secret of the home. Usage endpoint answers from Moonshot's servers.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: not used (maintainer ruling: outside what AI Juggler reads or sends today)

capabilities.name: Official SDK
capabilities.how: In-repo `@moonshot-ai/kimi-code-sdk` 0.21.1 (KimiHarness, Session, RPC client) is `private: true` and not on npm. The published `@moonshot-ai/kimi-agent-sdk` (Node 0.1.8, 2026-04-13; Python kimi-agent-sdk 0.0.5; Go) targets the archived Python Kimi CLI.
capabilities.limits: Use ACP (or the experimental server) instead; generic ACP SDKs (@agentclientprotocol/sdk, Rust agent-client-protocol) work.

capabilities.name: Plugins, skills, agents, commands
capabilities.how: Plugin = dir/zip with kimi.plugin.json (skills, agents, sessionStart.skill, systemPrompt(Path), mcpServers, hooks, commands). Installed via /plugins or marketplace into $KIMI_CODE_HOME/plugins/installed.json + plugins/managed/. Skills in $KIMI_CODE_HOME/skills, ~/.agents/skills, project; `--skills-dir` (replaces) per launch; `--agent`/`--agent-file` per launch. Rules: AGENTS.md (home, ~/.agents, project).
capabilities.limits: No per-launch plugin flag: installing means writing plugins/installed.json in the home. Plugin skills are invoked as <pluginID>:<skill> (2.3.x). Marketplace URL overridable (KIMI_CODE_PLUGIN_MARKETPLACE_URL).
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: rules file AGENTS.md is named in the ToolSpec; plugins not used

capabilities.name: Lifecycle hooks
capabilities.how: `[[hooks]]` in $KIMI_CODE_HOME/config.toml (event, matcher, command, timeout) or in a plugin manifest; stdin JSON with snake_case fields (hook_event_name, session_id, session_title, client_type, cwd, ...). Events: UserPromptSubmit (blocking; stdout appended to context), UserPromptQueued, PreToolUse (blocking), Stop (blocking; can make the model continue), TurnStarted, PostToolUse(/Failure), PermissionRequest, PermissionResult, SessionStart/End, SessionHeartbeat (60 s), Subagent*, TaskStarted, StopFailure, Interrupt, Pre/PostCompact, Notification.
capabilities.limits: Fail-open; only command hooks (no HTTP type found). Config-file only: no per-launch hooks flag, and the CLI reads a single user-level config, so injecting means writing the home's config.toml or a plugin. Desktop honours the same hooks.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: not used (state reports exist only for Claude Code)

capabilities.name: Our MCP server's tools
capabilities.how: Declare in $KIMI_CODE_HOME/mcp.json or project .kimi-code/mcp.json (`mcpServers`: stdio command/args/env/cwd, or url (+transport sse), headers, bearerTokenEnvVar, enabledTools, deferred), via a plugin, or per ACP session (session/new mcpServers). Tools appear as mcp__<server>__<tool>; content and structuredContent both passed to the model.
capabilities.limits: Client implements only tools/list + tools/call + ping (MCPClient interface); no resources, prompts, sampling or roots. Calls need approval unless `[[permission.rules]] allow mcp__juggler__*` in config.toml (or Ask-When-Needed mode). Servers added mid-session join only new sessions. clientInfo.name is 'kimi-code' (or KIMI_CODE_IDENTITY_SLUG, which AI Juggler must never set).
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: not used (agent_bridge implemented for Claude Code and Codex only)

capabilities.name: MCP elicitation
capabilities.how: The Kimi MCP client is constructed with no client capabilities (no elicitation handler) and registers no request handlers.
capabilities.limits: Negative evidence from source; ACP elicitation/create exists but is agent->ACP-client, not MCP server->agent.

capabilities.name: Server pushes into the session
capabilities.how: No MCP notification handling (no tools/list_changed); nothing an MCP server sends reaches the conversation outside a tool result. Closest documented push: a UserPromptSubmit hook's stdout is appended to the context; a blocked Stop hook can append a message to keep the model going.
capabilities.limits: Hook-based notes need a hook in the home's config.toml or a plugin. A Stop 'keep going' contradicts AI Juggler's never-decide rule.

capabilities.name: kimi-code:// URL scheme
capabilities.how: `kimi app [path]` opens `kimi-code://open?root=<abs path>&new=1` (opens a new desktop draft in that workspace). Composer also uses kimi-code://skill/... links internally.
capabilities.limits: Targets the Desktop app, not the CLI; only root and new parameters seen; no prompt parameter found; not documented as a public API beyond `kimi app`.

capabilities.name: Session files on disk
capabilities.how: $KIMI_CODE_HOME/session_index.jsonl (sessionId, sessionDir, workDir); sessions/<wd_slug_sha12>/<id>/state.json (title, lastPrompt, times, forkedFrom); agents/main/wire.jsonl = event journal: first line {type:metadata, protocol_version (1.5), created_at}, then {type, ...payload, time}. 67 record types in a generated manifest, e.g. turn.prompt {input, origin}, turn.ended {reason completed|cancelled|failed|blocked, error}, context.append_message {message}, usage.record {agentId, model, usage, usageScope}, interaction.request {kind approval|question|user_tool} / interaction.resolved. Sub-agents in agents/<sub>/wire.jsonl; locks/sessions/ occupancy locks.
capabilities.limits: Users are told not to edit sessions/; the wire manifest lives in the source tree (agent-core-v2/docs), not the user docs, with versioned migrations, so pin per protocol_version. Desktop sessions are in the same default home.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: kimi_sessions.rs reads session_index.jsonl + state.json (title, times, cwd, id) for the list, resume and linking; kimi_sessions/wire.rs reads agents/*/wire.jsonl incrementally (protocol 1.5 only) for live state and usage.record tokens

capabilities.name: Reading live output and state
capabilities.how: Deterministic, no model needed: tail wire.jsonl (turn.prompt/turn.ended for working/idle, interaction.request without interaction.resolved for 'needs you', usage.record for tokens); or hooks (TurnStarted, Stop, PermissionRequest, SessionHeartbeat); or ACP session/update when AI Juggler is the client; or the experimental server WS for server-owned sessions.
capabilities.limits: wire.jsonl schema is source-documented and versioned, not a user-docs contract; live capture needed (AJ-E1612).
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: TRANSCRIPT_WATCH on state.json; open sessions from locks/sessions/<id>.lock (pid), their state (working / needs you / idle) from the main agent's wire.jsonl turn.* and interaction.* records; unknown for another protocol version

capabilities.name: Run the TUI in our PTY
capabilities.how: AI Juggler launches `kimi` (needs_pty) and owns the PTY; the TUI (pi-tui) supports bracketed paste and has a paste-burst detector.
capabilities.limits: Screen parsing would need heuristics; use files/hooks for state instead.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: interactive launches, resume (`--session <id>`), login (`kimi login`) in a PTY

capabilities.name: Inserting a prompt
capabilities.how: No positional/initial prompt flag (extra args error out; only -p). Options: (1) PTY: bracketed-paste the text then send CR once the TUI is idle; a prompt sent while a turn runs is queued (UserPromptQueued); (2) ACP session/prompt for sessions AI Juggler drives; (3) server POST /sessions/{id}/prompts (+ :steer) for server-owned sessions.
capabilities.limits: PTY injection is deterministic in bytes but must check that no approval/question dialog is open (wire.jsonl interaction.request) or keystrokes land in the dialog. Cannot inject into a TUI-held session through the server (40931). Unattended injection on a membership account conflicts with 'interactive use only'.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: not used: Primed launch and Resume-with-delta are refused ('Kimi Code can't be started with a first message yet')

capabilities.name: Remote Control relay
capabilities.how: `kimi rc` / `kimi web --remote-control` / in-session `/remote-control` exposes the machine through code-rc.kimi.com|.ai for the same signed-in account (paid membership).
capabilities.limits: Goes through Moonshot's relay; one instance per machine; not an integration API for third parties.

capabilities.name: Import Claude Code/Codex sessions
capabilities.how: `kimi import-sessions` (interactive page) imports up to 100 recent Claude Code/Codex sessions (15/30 days) as Kimi sessions, honouring CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/CODEX_HOME; originals untouched.
capabilities.limits: Interactive only; one summarising first message, not a faithful replay.

capabilities.name: Quota feed
capabilities.how: GET /api/v1/oauth/usage on `kimi web` (limit5h, limit7d, monthTotal, monthCode usedRatio/resetAt; extraUsage); `/usage` in the TUI; per-turn tokens in wire.jsonl usage.record.
capabilities.limits: Server API experimental and answers from Moonshot; OAuth accounts only.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: plan quota not read; exact per-call tokens from wire.jsonl usage.record via usage_since (Measured, keyed by time, model and counts)

capabilities.name: A session's subagents
capabilities.how: state.json agents map ({type: sub, parentAgentId (always main), labels.parentAgentId (the real parent), labels.profileName}); agents/<agentId>/wire.jsonl per subagent (agent-0, agent-1, ...); the spawning agent's wire.jsonl holds subagent.spawned {subagentId, subagentName, description, runInBackground, parentToolCallId, parentAgentId}, subagent.started, and subagent.completed / failed / cancelled, each with time (ms). Server API GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/transcript?agent_id= and .../tasks.
capabilities.limits: Users are told not to edit sessions/; the server's transcript route resumes a cold session (writes). A rate-limit failure can leave no terminal record (then running/unknown). The subagent's conversation is an event journal, not read as a conversation yet.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: Subagents tab (AJ-E1520, 0.2): kimi_subagents lists them from the session folder, read-only; conversations not shown yet

entries.version_source: https://x.ai/cli/stable -> 1.0.70 and https://x.ai/cli/alpha -> 1.0.71 (same files on storage.googleapis.com/grok-build-public-artifacts/cli/); public source repo last synced 2026-09-29 at crate 1.0.45; `grok` not installed on this Mac

capabilities.name: Headless, JSON/stream output
capabilities.how: `grok -p|--single <prompt>` (also --prompt-json, --prompt-file), `--output-format plain|json|streaming-json|streaming-messages-json`, -r/-c/-s sessions, --cwd, --always-approve, --no-auto-update. json carries sessionId, stopReason, usage, modelUsage, total_cost_usd; streaming-json has text/thought/tool_call/tool_call_update/usage/plan/end/error lines.
capabilities.limits: docs.x.ai lists 3 formats; streaming-messages-json is in the repo guide only. 'Missing cost means unreported, not free.' AUP bans 'unauthorized automated or non-human' access, but Build docs say headless is 'ideal for scripts, automations, or integration into other apps'.

capabilities.name: ACP agent (stdio, WebSocket server, relay)
capabilities.how: `grok agent [--always-approve] stdio`; `grok agent serve --bind 127.0.0.1:2419 --secret <t>` (WebSocket, state kept across reconnects); `grok agent headless --grok-ws-url` (relay). session/new|load|prompt, session/update (agent_message_chunk, agent_thought_chunk, tool_call, tool_call_update, plan), permission requests, configOptions (model, reasoning_effort), _meta (rules, systemPromptOverride, agentProfile, yoloMode, autoMode, pluginDirs), x.ai/* extensions (fs, git, worktree, terminal, session fork, rewind, compact, auth).
capabilities.limits: Auth methods cached_token / xai.api_key. Whether a session can be loaded over ACP while a TUI holds it is not documented (U). Third parties (Vercel @ai-sdk/harness-grok-build 1.0.103, TanStack @tanstack/ai-grok-build 1.0.0) drive Grok Build through ACP.

capabilities.name: Official SDK
capabilities.how: Docs point to generic ACP SDKs (@agentclientprotocol/sdk, Rust agent-client-protocol, Python, Go, Kotlin). Source names an official 'grok-agent-sdk' (in-process @tool MCP servers, SDK hooks, --plugin-dir 'used by the Agent SDKs').
capabilities.limits: grok-agent-sdk not found on PyPI (name reserved by a third party, 0.0.0) or npm on 2026-10-27; treat as unreleased.

capabilities.name: Plugins, skills, marketplaces
capabilities.how: Plugin dir: skills/, commands/, agents/, hooks/hooks.json, .mcp.json, .lsp.json, optional plugin.json. Scopes: _meta.pluginDirs (one ACP session, auto-trusted), `grok agent --plugin-dir` (one agent process, auto-trusted, 'hooks and MCP servers activate without a prompt'), .grok/plugins (trust), $GROK_HOME/plugins, [plugins].paths. `grok plugin ...` CLI. Rules: AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md family, .grok/rules, $GROK_HOME/rules; `--rules` per launch.
capabilities.limits: --plugin-dir is an `grok agent` flag, not a TUI flag, and is ignored in leader mode. GROK_CONFIG/GROK_CONFIG_PATH overlay is allowlisted (models, features, toolset) and cannot add MCP servers, hooks or plugins. Also reads ~/.claude and ~/.cursor unless compat is off.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: rules not injected; AI Juggler sets GROK_CLAUDE_*/GROK_CURSOR_*_ENABLED=0 on every launch to stop ~/.claude and ~/.cursor bleed

capabilities.name: Lifecycle hooks
capabilities.how: JSON in $GROK_HOME/hooks/*.json, project .grok/hooks (trust), [[hooks.<Event>]] in config.toml, plugins, or registered by an ACP client. type command or http (POSTs the event envelope; ${VAR} expansion in url). Events: SessionStart/End, UserPromptSubmit (blocking), PreToolUse (blocking), PostToolUse(/Failure) (can add additionalContext / replace output), PermissionDenied, Stop/SubagentStop (blocking), StopFailure, StopCancelled, Notification (idle_prompt, permission_prompt, task_complete), Subagent*, Pre/PostCompact. Env GROK_SESSION_ID, GROK_HOOK_EVENT.
capabilities.limits: camelCase stdin envelope. An allowing UserPromptSubmit hook's stdout is discarded (no additionalContext). Writing to the default ~/.grok edits the user's setup.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: not used (state reports exist only for Claude Code)

capabilities.name: Our MCP server's tools
capabilities.how: [mcp_servers.<name>] in $GROK_HOME/config.toml (stdio or url, ${VAR}), project .grok/config.toml, `grok mcp add`, plugin .mcp.json, ACP session/new mcpServers. The model reaches MCP tools through search_tool/use_tool (deferred), and MCP resources through ListMcpResources/FetchMcpResource tools. Handles tools/list_changed and resources/list_changed. clientInfo name 'grok-shell-<server>'.
capabilities.limits: No prompts support found. Per-launch injection for the TUI only through the account's own GROK_HOME (AI Juggler-owned homes); GROK_CONFIG cannot add servers. Also loads ~/.claude.json MCPs unless GROK_CLAUDE_MCPS_ENABLED=0.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: not used (agent_bridge not implemented for Grok)

capabilities.name: MCP elicitation
capabilities.how: Client advertises elicitation form (with schema validation) and url modes when an interactive client is attached (not over the ACP transport); handles notifications/elicitation/complete. Also advertises the io.modelcontextprotocol/ui (MCP Apps) extension.
capabilities.limits: Not advertised in ACP-transport MCP; sampling and roots never advertised. From the 1.0.45 source sync, not the 1.0.70 binary.

capabilities.name: Server pushes into the session
capabilities.how: An MCP server can change its tool/resource lists live (list_changed handled) and ask the user via elicitation; it cannot start a turn. Hook-side: PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure can feed additionalContext; Stop can block.
capabilities.limits: No server-initiated prompt injection found.

capabilities.name: Session files on disk
capabilities.how: $GROK_HOME/sessions/<url-encoded cwd>/<uuidv7>/: summary.json (title, times, model, counts, parent), updates.jsonl (ACP session-update stream, authoritative for /resume), chat_history.jsonl, signals.json (turn_count, tool_call_count, error/cancel counts, context_tokens_used, context_window_tokens, ...), plan.json, rewind_points.jsonl, subagents/. Also $GROK_HOME/active_sessions.json: open TUI sessions {session_id, pid, cwd, opened_at}, pruned by PID. `grok usage <id>` gives token/cost totals; `grok sessions list|search`, `grok export`.
capabilities.limits: File field names are source-level, not user-docs contracts; active_sessions.json is internal. Source is 25 patch versions behind the shipping binary.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: grok_sessions.rs reads summary.json (title, times, model, parent) for the list, resume and linking; signals.json/updates.jsonl NOT read (tokens unknown)

capabilities.name: Reading live output and state
capabilities.how: Deterministic: tail updates.jsonl (ACP updates: tool_call status, agent chunks); hooks (Notification permission_prompt/idle_prompt, Stop, StopCancelled, StopFailure); active_sessions.json for which TUI sessions are open; ACP session/update when AI Juggler is the client.
capabilities.limits: Live capture still needed (AJ-E1612).

capabilities.name: Run the TUI in our PTY
capabilities.how: AI Juggler launches `grok` (needs_pty) and owns the PTY; the TUI handles bracketed paste (crossterm Event::Paste). `--no-alt-screen` runs inline. xAI's own ptyctl (headless PTY controller on alacritty_terminal) is an internal crate, not shipped.
capabilities.limits: Fullscreen mouse TUI: screen scraping is heuristic; use files/hooks.

capabilities.name: Inserting a prompt
capabilities.how: Positional initial prompt: `grok "fix the bug"` (also with --worktree; conflicts only with -p/--prompt-json/--prompt-file, so `--resume <id> "..."` should parse). Mid-session: PTY bracketed paste + CR; ACP session/prompt for ACP-driven sessions. The TUI dashboard can reply to its own live sessions (in-process).
capabilities.limits: Resume + positional prompt combination inferred from clap conflicts, not documented (I). A shared 'leader' process (`--leader`, ~/.grok/leader.sock, length-prefixed internal protocol) lets several clients share one backend, but it is internal and off by default.
capabilities.ai_juggler_uses: first message only: Primed -> `grok [--model m] -- <prompt>`, Resume with a delta -> `grok --resume <id> -- <delta>` (source 1.0.45, not yet live); nothing typed into a running session

capabilities.name: Quota feed
capabilities.how: Per-session tokens/cost: headless json/streaming usage, `grok usage <id>`, signals.json. Weekly pool %: only grok.com Settings and in-TUI /usage (internal FetchBilling).
capabilities.limits: No sanctioned pool feed; status line JSON 'contains no rate-limit data, quota, plan, or account information'.

capabilities.name: A session's subagents
capabilities.how: sessions/<cwd>/<session>/subagents/<subagent_id>/meta.json: subagent_type, description, status running|completed|failed|cancelled (a dead process's running is later rewritten to cancelled), started_at, completed_at, child_session_id (the subagent's own session folder, under its own cwd's group, which holds its own subagents/). updates.jsonl also carries _x.ai/session/update subagent_spawned / subagent_finished.
capabilities.limits: Field names are source-level (xai-org/grok-build, about a month older than the shipping CLI); background isn't in meta.json; the tool call id isn't persisted. The child's conversation is its ACP updates.jsonl, not read as a conversation yet.

entries.product: ZCode Agent CLI (zcode; bundled engine /Applications/ZCode.app/Contents/Resources/glm/zcode.cjs; source apps/zcode-cli in zai-org/ZCode)

capabilities.name: Headless prompt with JSON / NDJSON output
capabilities.how: zcode -p/--prompt <text> --cwd <dir> --mode build|edit|plan|yolo|guarded [--resume sess_...] with --json or --output-format text|json|stream-json. json = one object {sessionId, traceId, response, eventCount, projection, usage}; stream-json = NDJSON events ending in a type:"result" line. stdout = business output, stderr = diagnostics; exit 1 on errors.
capabilities.limits: Default mode for --prompt is yolo (auto-approve) - always pass --mode explicitly. --output-format is in the vendor usage docs (checked against source 2026-10-14) and the string is present in the installed 0.16.9 bundle, but 0.16.9 --help lists only --json, so stream-json on the installed build is unverified. Field shapes 'may change between builds'; unknown event types must be kept. Slash commands inside --prompt are not reliably executed.

capabilities.name: ZCode Protocol stdio app server
capabilities.how: zcode app-server --stdio (alias agent-server --stdio): strict NDJSON frames on stdout, logs on stderr. v1 methods: session/create, resume, list, read, messages, events, subscribe, send, stop, setModel, setThoughtLevel, setMode, close; workspace/readState; process/childProcesses (live MCP child pids). Server-to-client requests interaction/requestPermission and interaction/requestUserInput; session/subscribe returns gap events + optional snapshot; state.updated notifications. Schema: packages/shared/src/zcode-protocol(-v4)/index.ts.
capabilities.limits: Described by the vendor as the desktop's PRIVATE agent-server integration, not a public API; no versioning promise, schema moves with each build (v4 already). One server process per host connection; it does not attach to a session another process (the desktop) is running. Pin to the installed engine version and schema-validate every frame.

capabilities.name: Agent Client Protocol
capabilities.how: No ACP entry point: no acp/agent-client files in the zai-org/ZCode tree, not in --help, not in the 3.14-3.16 changelog.
capabilities.limits: Negative evidence only (search log: repo tree grep 'acp|agent-client', zcode --help, changelog, web search 2026-10-27). The app-server is ZCode's own protocol, not ACP.

capabilities.name: Programmatic SDK
capabilities.how: No published SDK: @zcode/cli is private:true; npm has no @zcode/* or @zai/* ZCode packages (zcode-cli@0.0.1 on npm is by an unaffiliated publisher).
capabilities.limits: The open-source monorepo (Apache-2.0) can be built (pnpm build:zcode), but that is not a supported SDK.

capabilities.name: Local web workbench (zcode --web)
capabilities.how: CLI distribution only: zcode --web [--workspace <dir>] [--port N] [--no-open]; listens on 127.0.0.1 with no token by default (token generated for non-local hosts; --token / --no-token).
capabilities.limits: Not in the app-bundled engine (0.16.9 help has no --web); needs a self-built distribution (pnpm build:zcode) since no official download URL is published (README uses a placeholder). Unauthenticated localhost server is a local security risk.

capabilities.name: Plugins, skills, commands, AGENTS.md
capabilities.how: Plugin = dir with .zcode-plugin/plugin.json (also reads .claude-plugin/ and .codex-plugin/), minimal manifest {name}; components commands, skills, hooks, mcpServers, agents; installed from marketplaces (GitHub repo, git URL, local dir, file); state in ~/.zcode/cli/config.json 'plugins'. Skills: ~/.zcode/skills, ~/.agents/skills, <repo>/.zcode/skills, <repo>/.agents/skills. Commands: same roots, commands/*.md, nested dir -> /a:b. Instructions: ~/.zcode/AGENTS.md then <repo>/AGENTS.md. CLI: zcode plugins list|install|uninstall|enable|disable|update|validate|marketplace, skills list, commands list (--json).
capabilities.limits: Manifest fields channels, lspServers, outputStyles, settings are recorded but NOT executed. User scope wins on name clashes. Built-in plugins can be disabled, not uninstalled.

capabilities.name: Hooks
capabilities.how: Seven events: SessionStart (startup|resume|clear|compact), UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop. Config: hooks.events.<Event> in ~/.zcode/cli/config.json or workspace config, or a plugin's hooks/hooks.json. type command (shell) or process (argv). Output JSON (strict schema) or exit codes 0 pass / 2 block; additionalContext injected into the conversation; PreToolUse/PermissionRequest may allow/ask/deny; Stop may request continuation (max 3). Env/template vars ${ZCODE_PROJECT_DIR}, ${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}.
capabilities.limits: Config-file hooks need hooks.enabled:true (off by default); any plugin hook auto-enables the runner. Hooks run inline (async ignored). Unknown keys fail validation. No Notification/SubagentStop/PreCompact events.

capabilities.name: Our MCP server: tools and resources
capabilities.how: Register under mcp.servers in <managed HOME>/.zcode/cli/config.json (fallback ~/.agents/mcp.json mcpServers) or workspace .zcode/config.json; stdio {command,args,cwd,env,enabled,timeoutMs} or http/sse {url,headers,oauth,timeoutMs}; protocolVersion auto|legacy|2026-07-28. Tools appear as mcp__<server>__<tool>; tools/list_changed honoured (refetch on next list); resources list/read/subscribe + resources/updated (mainly for MCP Apps UI, 3.15.1+); notifications/message logged; OAuth for http/sse.
capabilities.limits: Strict schema - an unknown key silently drops the server; no ${} expansion outside plugins; 30 s default timeout. MCP prompts are not consumed (no listPrompts in the client). Workspace-scoped servers now auto-connect without a trust prompt (security note). Desktop-managed MCP lists can override the file.

capabilities.name: MCP elicitation (form)
capabilities.how: Client declares elicitation:{form:{}} when the host provides a port; server elicitation/create is mapped to ZCode's user-question channel (string/number/integer/boolean/enum fields; flat schema).
capabilities.limits: Only attached when the host wires the port (TUI/desktop/app-server); in headless -p yolo runs there may be no one to answer (unverified). Only flat primitive schemas; url-mode elicitation not seen.
sources: local: grep of installed zcode.cjs 0.16.9 shows elicitation:{form:{...}} capability (2026-10-27)

capabilities.name: Server-initiated push into a running session
capabilities.how: No channel mechanism: plugin 'channels' field is recorded but not executed; the client handles only tools/resources list_changed, resources/updated and logging notifications - none becomes a user turn. Closest substitute: a UserPromptSubmit/SessionStart hook that fetches pending messages from AI Juggler and returns additionalContext (pull, at the agent's own turn boundaries).
capabilities.limits: Hook-based pull is inferred, untested; it adds context, it does not start a turn.

capabilities.name: Session store (SQLite) and logs
capabilities.how: SQLite at storage.sessionDbPath (default ~/.zcode/cli/db/db.sqlite; env ZCODE_SESSION_DB_PATH, legacy ZCODE_SESSION_DB). Core tables session / message (data JSON) / part (text, reasoning, file, tool, patch, compact), plus todo, session_entry, permission, input_history, model_usage/turn_usage/tool_usage; run state is in-memory only. Also ~/.zcode/cli/rollout/model-io-<sess>.jsonl (bounded: 64 MiB/file, last 3 sessions by default) and ~/.zcode/cli/log/zcode-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.
capabilities.limits: Vendor: 'the database structure is an implementation detail' - do not treat old SQL table layouts as a stable API; read-only connections only; copy via the SQLite backup API (WAL). model-io files may hold request headers (sensitive). 3.16.3 fixed data corruption from concurrent multi-session writes - never write.

capabilities.name: Resume, fork, rewind
capabilities.how: --resume sess_... or -c/--continue (latest for cwd; mutually exclusive); TUI /resume, /fork [latest|checkpointId], /rewind [latest|checkpointId] (workspace checkpoints), /compact; app-server session/resume.
capabilities.limits: Resume does not restore workspace/external state; -c is unsafe with concurrent sessions in one dir - always pass the id. Keep the same data dir and cwd.

capabilities.name: Per-account isolation
capabilities.how: Vendor batch recipe: per run set HOME, USERPROFILE and ZCODE_DATA_BASE_DIR to the run home with a whitelisted env (no inherited credentials); 'only changing sessionId or ZCODE_STORAGE_DIR is not enough'.
capabilities.limits: Credentials are a plaintext file under the home (~/.zcode/v2/credentials.json, 0600) - never read or copy it. Desktop shares the real ~/.zcode.

capabilities.name: Interactive TUI in a PTY
capabilities.how: zcode (or zcode tui) is an Ink full-screen TUI; AI Juggler can host it in portable-pty. Deterministic: process liveness, exit code, cwd, DB/log mtimes. Needs heuristics or a model: screen state (busy, waiting permission) - prefer hooks (PermissionRequest/Stop) or the DB for that.
capabilities.limits: Full-screen redraws make screen scraping fragile; locale (en-US/zh-CN) changes strings.

capabilities.name: Insert a prompt
capabilities.how: Supported: app-server session/send (sessions AI Juggler hosts), or a new headless turn with -p ... --resume <id>. Unsupported but possible: write keystrokes to an AI Juggler-owned PTY.
capabilities.limits: No way to insert into a session another process (desktop, user's terminal) is running; running -p --resume against a live session risks concurrent writers.

capabilities.name: Read output
capabilities.how: Hosted sessions: app-server session/events + subscribe, or stream-json. Any session: read-only SQLite message/part rows and model_usage. Per-run usage in JSON 'usage' (missing values are not zero).
capabilities.limits: SQLite layout not a stable API (version-gate on schema_migration); usage JSON is per run, not per account.

capabilities.name: Terms for a third-party launcher
capabilities.how: ZCode is itself an officially supported GLM Coding Plan tool, so the plan is consumed inside an official tool; Z.ai's own CLI docs describe driving the CLI from an external task launcher. AI Juggler never touches the plan API or credentials.
capabilities.limits: Coding Plan: 'only within officially supported tools', no account sharing or multi-user access, risk control up to bans. ZCode agreement (updated 2026-06-15): no improper multi-account use (s3.2), personal use only (s3.3), non-commercial personal use unless paid/other agreement (s6.2), no use 'via deep links, scraping, social bots, spiders or other automated means', no reverse engineering (s4.3). A launcher of the official binary is not addressed head-on - maintainer ruling needed.
