entries.product: ZCode.app (Electron, dev.zcode.app)

capabilities.name: zcode:// deep links
capabilities.how: zcode://workspace/open?path=<url-encoded absolute dir> opens a local folder as a workspace (cold start buffered until renderer ready; same path used by the auto-installed Finder service ~/Library/Services/Open in ZCode.workflow). Other hosts: oauth/callback, payment/callback, share/import?code=.
capabilities.limits: No route to open a given session, focus a task, or send a prompt. Rejected when allowOpenWorkspace=false. Deep-link-opened projects auto-connect their workspace MCP servers (trust boundary doc).
sources: local: Info.plist CFBundleURLSchemes=zcode; app.asar contains OpenWorkspacePath; ~/Library/Services/Open in ZCode.workflow present (2026-10-27)

capabilities.name: Desktop agent channel
capabilities.how: The desktop spawns the bundled zcode-cli as a private stdio agent server (app-server --stdio) per host connection; there is no socket or port another app can attach to. ZCODE_AGENT_SERVER_COMMAND overrides the agent command for dev builds only.
capabilities.limits: Replacing the desktop's agent command would be a hack (and against the architecture standard); not an integration surface.

capabilities.name: Read desktop sessions
capabilities.how: Desktop sessions are held by the bundled CLI server, so they land in the same ~/.zcode/cli/db/db.sqlite (+ ~/.zcode/v2/tasks-index.sqlite for tasks/automations/off-peak tasks). Read-only SQLite + file watching.
capabilities.limits: Same 'implementation detail' caveat as the CLI; real ~/.zcode (no isolation); read-only walks only on the maintainer's real setup.

capabilities.name: Insert a prompt into the desktop
capabilities.how: No supported external input path. Vendor-only remote paths exist (Remote Control from the phone with account login, Bot Channel via WeChat/Feishu/Telegram) - cloud relays, not for a local manager.
capabilities.limits: UI automation (Accessibility/AppleScript) would be fragile and ToS-sensitive ('automated means').

capabilities.name: Our MCP server in the desktop
capabilities.how: Same files as the CLI (~/.zcode/cli/config.json mcp.servers, workspace .zcode/config.json); Settings -> MCP shows status; import from Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, ~/.agents/mcp.json; MCP Apps (UI resources) since 3.15.1; elicitation shown as a user question.
capabilities.limits: Desktop-managed server lists can override the file; desktop expects canonical fields (env not environment, string command). Restart the session after edits. Writing the user's real config needs approval.

capabilities.name: Push into a desktop session
capabilities.how: As the CLI: no channels; notifications do not create turns.
capabilities.limits: Hook additionalContext pull is the only substitute (inferred).

capabilities.name: Plugins, skills, hooks in the desktop
capabilities.how: Settings -> Plugin Management (Installed/Discover, marketplace since 3.16.2), Skills, Subagents; same file roots as the CLI. A local marketplace can carry an AI Juggler plugin (hooks + MCP).
capabilities.limits: Plugin hooks run regardless of marketplace (no trust gate) - ship only what the user approves.

capabilities.name: Observe the desktop
capabilities.how: Process list (bundle id dev.zcode.app, child zcode.cjs app-server), read-only DB, daily JSONL logs, hooks from an approved plugin.
capabilities.limits: Window/tab to session mapping not exposed; 'Go to it' can only activate the app or open a workspace by path.

entries.product: Gemini CLI (@google/gemini-cli, Apache-2.0)
entries.version_source: https://registry.npmjs.org/@google/gemini-cli (dist-tags, 2026-10-27); not installed locally (which gemini: not found)

capabilities.name: Which sign-ins still work
capabilities.how: Since 2026-06-18 Gemini CLI stopped serving free Gemini Code Assist for individuals and Google AI Pro/Ultra (consumer) logins; successor is Antigravity CLI (agy). Still served: Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise (Google Cloud terms), paid Gemini API keys and Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform API keys (Vertex). geminicli.com banner: 'Unpaid tier and Google One users: Gemini CLI was replaced by Antigravity CLI on June 18th, 2026.'
capabilities.limits: Repo docs (quota-and-pricing.md, tos-privacy.md) still list the consumer tiers - stale; the website banner and Google blog govern. Free-tier Gemini API key status after the sunset is unclear (blog says 'paid' keys).

capabilities.name: Headless with JSON / stream-json
capabilities.how: gemini -p <prompt> (or non-TTY stdin) --output-format text|json|stream-json; json = {response, stats, error?}; stream-json = JSONL events init (session id, model), message, tool_use, tool_result, error, result (aggregated stats, per-model tokens). Exit codes 0, 1, 42 input error, 53 turn limit. -r latest|<index>|<uuid> with a prompt continues a session; --approval-mode default|auto_edit|yolo|plan.
capabilities.limits: Folder trust gates workspace settings (--skip-trust / GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE for headless); model.maxSessionTurns exits non-interactive runs with error.

capabilities.name: Agent Client Protocol
capabilities.how: gemini --acp (--experimental-acp is now a deprecated alias): JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio. Methods initialize (client may register its MCP server), authenticate, newSession, loadSession, prompt, cancel, setSessionMode, unstable_setSessionModel; session/request_permission to the client with _meta['gemini-cli'].mcp {server_name, tool_name}; file-system proxy through the client. Listed in the ACP Agent Registry (Zed, JetBrains).
capabilities.limits: Sessions created via ACP are driven by the client - AI Juggler would own the UI for them; it cannot attach to a user's interactive terminal session. unstable_* methods may change. cli-reference.md still documents only --experimental-acp (doc lag).

capabilities.name: SDK / A2A server
capabilities.how: packages/sdk (@google/gemini-cli-sdk, GeminiCliAgent.sendStream) exists in the repo but is not on npm (registry 404). @google/gemini-cli-a2a-server 0.65.0 is published (bin gemini-cli-a2a-server), marked 'experimental and under active development'. @google/gemini-cli-core is published.
capabilities.limits: No stable SDK; A2A server experimental; embedding core is unsupported.

capabilities.name: Extensions, custom commands, skills, GEMINI.md
capabilities.how: Extension = dir with gemini-extension.json {name, version, mcpServers, contextFileName, excludeTools, settings[] (envVar), ...} plus commands/*.toml, hooks, skills; gemini extensions install|link|enable|disable|update|validate|new. Custom commands: TOML in ~/.gemini/commands and <repo>/.gemini/commands. Skills: gemini skills install|link. Context: hierarchical GEMINI.md.
capabilities.limits: settings.json MCP entries override same-named extension servers; extension env is sanitised unless declared.

capabilities.name: Hooks
capabilities.how: settings.json hooks: BeforeTool, AfterTool, BeforeAgent, AfterAgent, BeforeModel, BeforeToolSelection, AfterModel, SessionStart, SessionEnd, Notification (ToolPermission), PreCompress. stdin JSON includes session_id, transcript_path, cwd, hook_event_name; stdout JSON; exit 2 blocks. BeforeAgent/SessionStart additionalContext; AfterAgent deny -> reason becomes a new prompt (retry).
capabilities.limits: Only type 'command'; Notification and SessionEnd are observe-only; SessionEnd not awaited.

capabilities.name: Our MCP server: tools, prompts, resources
capabilities.how: settings.json mcpServers (user ~/.gemini or $GEMINI_CLI_HOME/.gemini, project .gemini/settings.json, or extension); stdio/SSE/streamable HTTP; trust, includeTools/excludeTools, timeout (default 600 000 ms), OAuth (RFC 9207 issuer checks), Google credentials/SA impersonation; gemini mcp add|remove|list. Prompts become slash commands; resources via @server://uri and list_mcp_resources/read_mcp_resource tools; tools/resources/prompts list_changed handled; progress notifications shown; client offers roots.
capabilities.limits: mcp.allowed / --allowed-mcp-server-names can exclude us; env sanitisation redacts secrets unless explicitly set.

capabilities.name: MCP elicitation
capabilities.how: Client registers only the roots capability. PR #28089 (form + url elicitation) closed unmerged 2026-07-07; issue #28074 closed not_planned 2026-09-06.
capabilities.limits: A server calling elicitation/create gets method-not-found (cf. #22249).

capabilities.name: Push into a running session
capabilities.how: No prompt push. Context-only push exists via the IDE companion interface: an MCP-over-HTTP server announced in os.tmpdir()/gemini/ide/gemini-ide-server-<PID>-<PORT>.json {port, workspacePath, authToken, ideInfo{name,displayName}} (or GEMINI_CLI_IDE_SERVER_PORT / GEMINI_CLI_IDE_PID) can send ide/contextUpdate (open files, cursor, selection; 10 files / 16 KB) and offer openDiff/closeDiff.
capabilities.limits: Designed for IDE companions; using it from AI Juggler (as the parent 'IDE') is inferred, untested, and only adds context. Hook pull (BeforeAgent additionalContext) is the other substitute.

capabilities.name: Session transcripts
capabilities.how: ~/.gemini/tmp/<project_hash>/chats/session-<timestamp>-<shortId>.jsonl (subagents under a parent-id subdir), append-only JSONL: metadata {sessionId, projectHash, startTime, lastUpdated, summary, kind main|subagent}, message records (user|gemini|info|error|warning; toolCalls; tokens {input, output, cached, thoughts, tool, total}), $set metadata updates, $patch records, $rewindTo. Legacy .json files are normalised. gemini --list-sessions / --delete-session; hooks receive transcript_path.
capabilities.limits: Internal format (not a documented contract) - parse tolerantly. Default retention deletes sessions after 30 days (general.sessionRetention). Root moves with GEMINI_CLI_HOME.

capabilities.name: Checkpointing and rewind
capabilities.how: general.checkpointing.enabled (default off): shadow git in ~/.gemini/history/<project_hash>, checkpoint JSON in ~/.gemini/tmp/<project_hash>/checkpoints; /restore [file]; /rewind; /resume save|list|resume <tag> chat checkpoints.
capabilities.limits: Off by default; settings-only since 0.11.0.

capabilities.name: Per-account isolation
capabilities.how: GEMINI_CLI_HOME=<managed root> (CLI creates .gemini inside); GEMINI_API_KEY / Vertex env per child; GEMINI_CLI_TRUSTED_FOLDERS_PATH.
capabilities.limits: Google-login OAuth tokens land under the home (or keychain) - never read them; consumer login is no longer served anyway.

capabilities.name: Interactive CLI in a PTY
capabilities.how: Host gemini in portable-pty; deterministic signals from the JSONL transcript, hooks (Notification ToolPermission = waiting for approval; AfterAgent = turn done) and exit codes; screen parsing only as fallback.
capabilities.limits: Ink TUI redraws; screen text is not a contract.

capabilities.name: Insert a prompt
capabilities.how: Supported: ACP prompt (AI Juggler-hosted sessions), or a headless turn gemini -r <uuid> -p <text>. PTY keystrokes for an owned interactive session (unsupported but workable). -i <prompt> seeds an interactive start.
capabilities.limits: No insertion into a session another process runs; concurrent -r on a live session may conflict (unverified).

capabilities.name: Read output and usage
capabilities.how: stream-json result stats (per-model tokens), transcript token fields, /stats in-session, optional local OTLP telemetry (telemetry.target local + outfile).
capabilities.limits: No account-quota feed for remaining Cloud/API tiers (see gemini.md s4).

capabilities.name: Terms for a third-party launcher
capabilities.how: Gemini CLI is Apache-2.0; service terms depend on auth (Code Assist Standard/Enterprise -> Google Cloud terms; API key -> Gemini API terms; Vertex -> GCP terms).
capabilities.limits: 'Directly accessing the services powering Gemini CLI ... using third-party software ... (for example, using OpenClaw with Gemini CLI OAuth) is a violation' - AI Juggler must only launch the official binary, never reuse its OAuth. For the consumer successor, Antigravity's FAQ says wrapping agy in third-party apps and automating account rotation are not supported on consumer plans.

entries.product: Kiro CLI (kiro-cli)
entries.notes:
- CLI latest 2.34.2 (vendor manifest https://desktop-release.q.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/latest/manifest.json, VP); changelog newest 2.34.0 (2026-10-23). IDE latest 1.4.26 (2026-10-22, VP https://kiro.dev/changelog/ide/).
- V3 is NOT the default yet: still "early release" alongside 2.x; opt-in startup prompt in a gradual rollout since 2.30.0 (VP https://kiro.dev/docs/cli/v3/, changelog 2.30). 2.34.0's default ACP engine is v2 (VS GH#12118). Changelog says V3 default "with CLI 3.0 at the end of October".
- ACP launch: `kiro-cli acp --agent-engine=v3 --auth-method=cli|client` (VP). V3 refuses --agent/--model/--effort/--trust-*; use session/set_config_option (model, effortLevel); no session/set_model in V3. v2 has session/set_model but no session/list (GH#7098 open).
- Register session/update before create/load: live updates not buffered (VP). Permission options must be echoed exactly; never synthesize (VP).
- MCP: tools, resources(+templates), prompts, elicitation (form/URL; CLI local V3 from 2.34; IDE), tools/list_changed (CLI 2.14+). Not documented: sampling, roots, MCP Apps; progress not rendered (VS GH#10134). Names ≤64 incl. server prefix, ^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$. Untrusted workspace: every MCP call asks, even autoApprove. No MCP push-into-session (NE).
- Hooks: v1 JSON .kiro/hooks/*.json; global ~/.kiro/hooks V3 only. Triggers SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostFile{Create,Save,Delete}, Pre/PostTaskExec, Stop (+SessionEnd V3). Exit 0 stdout → agent context; Stop {"decision":"block"} continues. Exit-code docs conflict (exit-codes page: only 2 blocks; hooks/actions: any non-zero). Workspace Trust (2.33.0) gates hooks/agents/MCP/steering in interactive V3.
- Output/input: KIRO_ACP_RECORD_PATH records TUI ACP traffic to JSONL (VP; may carry token traffic — keep private). OSC 7501 + title states (VP; pending ask reported as error, VS GH#11987). /chat save-via-script sends session JSON to a script (VP). Session live in one process only ("Session is active in another process") — can't attach to a user's running TUI (VP). Shell integration exec's kiro-cli-term; guard PROCESS_LAUNCHED_BY_KIRO=1 (VS GH#11170).
- Fresh-install `kiro-cli acp` blocks session/new ~66 s downloading an 83 MB embedding model (VS GH#12118).
- Desktop (IDE): agent is built-in extension kiro.kiro-agent using ACP internally (VS, maint); no documented way for external ACP agent or extension API to drive the agent (NE). URL scheme: kiro://kiro.mcp/add?name=&config= and kiro://kiro.powers/add?name= (VP, from kiro.dev launch-page JS), confirmation dialog; no prompt/open link (NE). "Open with Kiro CLI" hand-off (VP). Status dots on tabs. KIRO_HOME in IDE: NE.
- Terms: pricing/FAQ unchanged — "ACP compatible IDEs" allowed; "third-party automation harnesses (such as OpenClaw)" routing outside native interfaces not permitted. ACP docs invite "custom integration" (VP). AWS Service Terms updated 2026-10-22, nothing on harnesses. Customer Agreement §6.4 bans reverse engineering. Reading: spawning native kiro-cli acp is the defensible path; ask AWS.

entries.product: Hermes Agent CLI/TUI (Nous Research, `hermes`, repo NousResearch/hermes-agent, MIT)
entries.version_source: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/releases/tag/v0.22.5 (GitHub API, published 2026-10-23); not installed on this Mac (`type -a hermes`: not found)

capabilities.name: One-shot runs with JSONL / usage report
capabilities.how: `hermes chat --oneshot -q|--query-file - --format stream-json` (events system/text/tool_use/tool_result/result with tokens, session_id, exit_code); `hermes -z <prompt> --usage-file <path>` (final text only + JSON usage report incl. auxiliary calls); `--source tool` keeps runs out of user pickers; `--ignore-user-config --ignore-rules` for isolated runs
capabilities.limits: Since 0.21 `-q` on a real TTY seeds an interactive session instead of exiting: always pass `--oneshot` (or non-TTY stdio). Exit codes differ between `chat` (1 = failed) and `-z` (2 = failed, 1 = no text). Still a client of the profile gateway (gateway must be up).

capabilities.name: Per-home gateway daemon = sole session writer
capabilities.how: `hermes gateway ensure --json [--timeout N]` discovers or starts the home's session runtime without installing a service (JSON state/reason_code/endpoint, never tickets); `hermes gateway status|list|stop`. CLI, TUI, Desktop, ACP, API server and cron are all clients over `/api/ws`.
capabilities.limits: Gateway outlives the app, has no idle shutdown. Multiplexing is now the default: one host gateway serves every profile under ~/.hermes/profiles; a HERMES_HOME outside profiles/ is a 'real boundary' and gets its own gateway. `gateway stop` asks y/N when turns run (scripts need --yes). Lifecycle ownership must be designed.

capabilities.name: TUI gateway JSON-RPC (full host protocol)
capabilities.how: JSON-RPC over stdio or WebSocket: session.create/list/resume/activate/history/status/usage/interrupt/steer/branch, prompt.submit, command.dispatch, events message.delta/complete, tool.start/complete; server->client requests approval/clarify/sudo/secret (client must call client.capabilities {server_requests:true}). Resuming a live session attaches another subscriber (multi-viewer).
capabilities.limits: Authentication for a third-party local client goes through the same-user private control socket (`session-ticket`, 30 s one-use ticket) documented only in developer-guide internals; the stdio launch command for an external host is not documented as a public CLI. Breaking changes are announced in docs (e.g. client.capabilities became mandatory).

capabilities.name: Agent Client Protocol server
capabilities.how: `hermes acp` / `hermes-acp` (JSON-RPC over stdio; stdout reserved): initialize/authenticate, session new/load/resume/fork/list/cancel, prompt, streamed chunks, tool calls, permission requests (allow_once/allow_session/allow_always). `hermes acp --check`. Editor-supplied mcpServers on session/new attach to that session.
capabilities.limits: Needs the `acp` extra installed into the checkout (`pm.sync_venv(['acp'])`). ACP now runs as a viewer of the gateway daemon. Curated `hermes-acp` toolset (no messaging/cron). Uses the home's configured provider; no auth store of its own.

capabilities.name: OpenAI-compatible HTTP API with runs
capabilities.how: `http://127.0.0.1:8642/v1`: chat/completions, responses, runs (POST, GET status, SSE events, approval, steer, stop), capabilities; X-Hermes-Session-Id header
capabilities.limits: Needs API_SERVER_KEY configured in the home's .env (writing a secret into the user's home); does not serve /api/ws; steer only while status=running.

capabilities.name: Official SDK
capabilities.how: No published client SDK package; in-process Python embed via `run_agent.AIAgent`; protocols above are the integration surface
capabilities.limits: Python-only embed, not usable from Rust; would import Hermes' venv

capabilities.name: Account limits without a session
capabilities.how: `hermes usage [--provider openai-codex|anthropic|openrouter] --json` (provider, plan, windows[used_percent,resets_at], fetched_at; keys stable, additive)
capabilities.limits: Codex/Anthropic windows come from feeds codex.md section 9 judged unsanctioned for AI Juggler: show only as Hermes-reported on a Hermes account. Nous Portal not listed as a usage provider.

capabilities.name: Per-account home
capabilities.how: `HERMES_HOME=<dir>` (resolver: context override > HERMES_HOME > ~/.hermes); profiles under ~/.hermes/profiles/<name>; spawners must pass HERMES_HOME explicitly; changing HOME is not safe
capabilities.limits: A home outside profiles/ runs its own gateway (needs `--force` for service installs). Nous Portal ToS 5.1: one account per person.

capabilities.name: Keeping Hermes off managed ~/.codex and Claude homes
capabilities.how: Set `auth.adopt_external_logins: false` in the Hermes home's config.yaml (default true: Hermes otherwise borrows and REFRESHES ~/.codex/auth.json and Claude Code's credentials file or the 'Claude Code-credentials' Keychain item, and since #98334 writes refreshes back into that Keychain item). Set CODEX_HOME (and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) in the Hermes process env to a Hermes-owned empty dir: token import, the Codex app-server runtime's config.toml writes and `hermes sessions import --from codex|claude` all honour them. Don't install `agent-importers` / don't run `import-agent` or `--sync` against managed homes; audit `$HERMES_HOME/import-sync.json`.
capabilities.limits: The Keychain read uses a fixed service name, so only adopt_external_logins=false stops it. import-agent auto-detects ~/.codex/~/.claude/~/.cursor (CODEX_HOME support for import-agent not documented). `hermes setup` offers the import on fresh installs. `hermes auth add openai-codex` still offers to import an existing Codex login interactively.

capabilities.name: Plugins and catalog
capabilities.how: `hermes plugins install|list|update|remove`, official catalog (NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins), Python plugins under $HERMES_HOME/plugins/<name> with plugin hooks; portable agent plugin packages (plugin.json) can ship MCP servers; `hermes://plugin/install` links
capabilities.limits: In-process Python (no isolation). Several former core commands moved to plugins in 0.22.4/0.22.5 (agent-importers, mcp-serve).

capabilities.how: $HERMES_HOME/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, `hermes skills`, `-s/--skills` preload, catalog and `hermes://skill/install?identifier=` links
capabilities.limits: Per home; import of Claude/Codex skills only via agent-importers plugin

capabilities.how: config.yaml `hooks:` shell hooks (any language; JSON on stdin with hook_event_name, session_id, cwd, profile; stdout JSON block/modify/approve/context; exit 2 = block, Claude-Code compatible) for pre/post_tool_call, pre/post_llm_call, on_session_start/end, subagent_start/stop, pre_approval_request, on_human_input_request and more; gateway hooks ~/.hermes/hooks/<name>/HOOK.yaml

capabilities.limits: Starts a NEW run per event, not injection into an existing live session; needs platforms.webhook with a public HTTPS URL (servers reject plain HTTP); working-group draft

capabilities.name: Sessions in SQLite
capabilities.how: $HERMES_HOME/state.db (SQLite WAL, schema_version 31): sessions (source, model, cwd, git_branch, tokens incl. cache/reasoning, billing_provider, estimated/actual_cost_usd, title, profile_name, archived...) and messages (role, content, tool_calls JSON, reasoning, message_uid...). Open read-only (mode=ro); `hermes sessions export <out> [--session-id]` writes JSONL; `hermes sessions list|stats`, `hermes insights`
capabilities.limits: Gateway is the only writer; read-only openers may still touch WAL/SHM sidecars; schema evolves (columns added declaratively); compaction rotates physical rows (use message_uid)

capabilities.how: Gateway: session.resume({session_id}) then prompt.submit({session_id, submission_id, text}) (queued/steered per busy_input_mode) or session.steer; API server: POST /v1/runs/{id}/steer; resume a saved session with `hermes chat -r <id>`

capabilities.limits: Also discovers ~/.claude/skills and $CODEX_HOME/skills (fallback ~/.codex/skills) plus repo .claude/.codex skills: managed homes leak in unless CODEX_HOME points elsewhere, the preference/rollout gate is off, or `--no-foreign-personal-context` is passed

capabilities.name: Hooks
capabilities.how: 17 events (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PostToolBatch, PreLLMCall, PostLLMCall, PreCompact, PostCompact, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, Notification, Stop, StopFailure, SessionEnd) in .muse/hooks.json, user settings or managed_hooks_path; MSP hook/list
capabilities.limits: Wire format not documented; hooks run outside the sandbox with a cleared env; project hooks need folder trust

capabilities.name: Rules
capabilities.how: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .agents/AGENTS.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md per directory up to .git; `muse init`
capabilities.limits: Untrusted workspaces no longer inherit project rules (1.4.13)

capabilities.name: Our MCP server
capabilities.how: settings.json mcp_servers (stdio command/args/env/framing or streamable_http url/headers; mode required|optional; ${VAR}); MUSE_SESSION_ID passed to stdio servers; OAuth via `muse mcp login`; per-session servers through MSP session/start config.mcpServers (capability sessionMcp) - no settings file edit needed
capabilities.limits: Only tools documented; resources/prompts/list_changed/progress not documented; default mode required aborts the run if our server fails; MCP tools not sandboxed

capabilities.name: MCP elicitation
capabilities.how: Not found in docs, changelog or MSP schema; Muse's own request_user_input question tool exists (answered via userInput/answer)
capabilities.limits: Not found by this search

capabilities.name: Push into a live session
capabilities.how: Session messaging: `muse session-message list --json` and `muse session-message send --target <uuid|name> [--in-reply-to] [--display-context <json>] [--json] < body`; delivery steers the active turn, queues, or notify-only, and can wake an idle recipient
capabilities.limits: Docs cover only session-to-session use; peer text is 'unverified agent-provided data' (may prompt for approval, cannot approve tools); 8,192 bytes plain text; macOS/Linux, interactive sessions only, rollout-gated; experimental peerMessaging capability; whether a non-session sender is accepted is unknown

capabilities.name: Session logs
capabilities.how: Observed: ~/.local/share/muse/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/<uuid>/session.jsonl (+ peer-history sqlite, tool-outputs, subagent, workflows) and session-index.db. Offline readers: `muse export --session <uuid|path> --out <file> [--redacted]` (one JSON doc, export_schema_version 1) and `muse trace inspect --session-log <jsonl> --format json`
capabilities.limits: Path and raw format undocumented (layout from a names-only listing); export default output is RAW incl. encrypted reasoning; prefer MSP session/list + session/read (read without attaching)

capabilities.name: Live output
capabilities.how: MSP item/started|delta|completed, turn/*, session/statusChanged, session/tokenUsage, session/contextUsage; view/subscribe attaches a read-only live view at a cursor without taking a lease; session/list includes sessions another process (TUI) uses
capabilities.limits: Resuming a session another process uses is refused (sessionInUse) while it is in use; session/leave hands it over

capabilities.name: Insert a prompt
capabilities.how: Sessions we host: turn/start, turn/steer, turn/unqueue; sessions owned by an open TUI: session messaging (above) or PTY input
capabilities.limits: No MSP write into a session another host holds

capabilities.name: PTY-wrapped TUI, deterministic fixtures
capabilities.how: Interactive `muse` in a PTY; `--provider echo --echo-delay-ms <ms>` gives a deterministic echo reply with no model or account (fixtures and conformance tests); `--provider local` also exists
capabilities.limits: Screen parsing still fragile; OSC 7501 status sequences exist (1.4.11) but undocumented

capabilities.name: Terms for third-party control
capabilities.how: SDK repo invites programmatic control ('SDK and documentation for how to programmatically control Muse Code'). Subscriptions: 'This credential is for use with Muse Code only', 'works only through the Muse Code CLI'; governed by Meta Subscription ToS, Meta Model API ToS and AUP
capabilities.limits: Driving the CLI's own serve/exec keeps traffic in Muse Code (inferred fine); never extract or reuse the subscription credential elsewhere; no multi-account clause found; a secondary tracker lists a no-sharing-of-API-keys clause

entries.product: No official Meta Muse Code desktop app
entries.version_source: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/ (describes 'coding agent for the terminal and CI'); web search 2026-10-27

capabilities.name: Official desktop app
capabilities.how: Not found by this search. The changelog mentions 'the desktop app' (1.4.10 conversation switching between desktop app and terminal) and 'Desktop and other connected clients' (1.4.13) without naming one. Third-party GUIs exist (muse-desktop by EtienneLescot, AFK Pilot, Paseo), all wrapping the CLI and not from Meta; musecodes.io warns that 'desktop app' downloads are not from Meta
capabilities.limits: If Meta ships one, it would likely be an MSP client of the same `muse` host (inferred from the changelog wording)
